reader.requirement: At --std 85 the mnemonic-name of a SPECIAL-NAMES entry whose implementor-name is an external switch is legal only as the operand of a format 3 SET statement; its use in ACCEPT, DISPLAY, WRITE ADVANCING, SEND ADVANCING or as a data reference or condition must be refused.

edition-consulted.switches: Prints2002 (Edition.Year >= 2002) picks which edition's rule text the COBOL6171 message quotes; the switch-mnemonic refusal itself is the same test at every edition

reader.edition-search: Read SwitchBindSet, MnemonicDevice, FeatureAdvancing, ScreenSendAdvancing and BindImplementorNameEntry and grepped them and ImplementorNames.cs for Edition/Year/DialectLevel: the only edition consultation is the SEND message's quoted text; the mnemonic-kind tests are edition-blind, as the rule is the same in 1985 and later editions.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness proves only the legal SET half (format 3, ON/OFF, two receivers); none of the refusal half (ACCEPT, DISPLAY, WRITE, SEND, data reference) is exercised

probes.expected: accepted: SET SW3 TO ON then SW3-ON is true (GR3)

probes.printed: error COBOL0817: DISPLAY UPON 'SW3': 'SW3' is the mnemonic-name of the switch-name 'SWITCH-3', not of a device-name
probes.expected: refused: switch mnemonic only in SET

probes.printed: error COBOL0817: ACCEPT FROM 'SW3': ... not of a device-name
error COBOL2243: WRITE ADVANCING 'SW3': 'SW3' is the mnemonic-name of the switch-name 'SWITCH-3'
error COBOL6171: SEND ADVANCING AFTER ADVANCING SW3: §1985:XIV.3.6.3 SR4 ...

probes.expected: accepted: control for the SEND probe
refused: a mnemonic-name is not a data item

probes.printed: error COBOL2318: 'SW3' is used as a condition, but it is the mnemonic-name 'SW3' of a switch
probes.expected: refused: status is tested via condition-names

probes.printed: error COBOL1757: SET 'CON' TO ON ... 'CON' is the mnemonic-name of the device-name 'CONSOLE'
probes.expected: refused (SR2 dual: a device mnemonic is not a SET operand)
accepted: control, device mnemonic in DISPLAY

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.4.5.3 SR1  (4.5.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1
OK  §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR3  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3
OK  §1985:VI.4.5.3 SR2  (4.5.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2

reader.notes: Every statement that takes a mnemonic-name (ACCEPT, DISPLAY, WRITE, SEND) checks the mnemonic's system-name kind and refuses a switch's; SET format 3 accepts it and works. A switch mnemonic used as a data name or a condition is also refused. The diagnostics other than SEND's quote §2023 clause numbers even at --std 85 (wording only).

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 aimed at what the reader did not try: class c (1985 IPC nesting, §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR1) c2_nested_set: a contained program SETs the containing program's SW3 TO ON and tests SW3-ON, the outer then sees it: printed 'INNER ON / OUTER SEES ON' (accepted, as GR1 requires); c2_nested_disp: DISPLAY UPON SW3 in the contained program refused COBOL0817. Other SET forms with the switch mnemonic: SET SW3 TO TRUE refused COBOL1639, SET SW3 UP BY 1 refused COBOL1639, SET IX TO SW3 refused COBOL1639, SET N TO SW3 refused COBOL2326, SET SW3-ON TO TRUE refused COBOL1757; SET SW3 SW3 TO OFF (format 3, repeated operand) RAN. STRING ... INTO SW3 and INSPECT SW3 refused COBOL1639. Grepped SetAlterBinder.cs and SpecialNamesBinder.cs for Edition/DialectLevel/ConstructRegistry: no edition arm on the switch-mnemonic path. Cite: OK §1985:VI.4.5.3 SR1; OK §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR1 'All clauses specified in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph for a program also apply to programs contained within that program'. Wording only: SET N TO SW3 is refused with an index-name message (SR4) rather than naming SW3 as a switch mnemonic.
